pairs: Pilate then took Jesus into custody and scourged him.
Et milites plectentes coronam de spinis,
And the soldiers, plaiting a crown of thorns,
And they put a purple garment around him.

Then Pilate went outside again, and he said to them:
“Behold, I am bringing him out to you,
ut cognoscatis quia nullam invenio in eo causam.
so that you may realize that I find no case against him.”
bearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment.)
Cum ergo vidissent eum pontifices et ministri,
when the high priests and the attendants had seen him,
ego enim non invenio in eo causam.
For I find no case against him.”
The Jews answered him, “We have a law,
et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit.
he ought to die, for he has made himself the Son of God.”
Cum ergo audisset Pilatus hunc sermonem,
Therefore, when Pilate had heard this word,
And he entered into the praetorium again.
Jesus autem responsum non dedit ei.
But Jesus gave him no response.
nescis quia potestatem habeo crucifigere te,
Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you,
and I have authority to release you?”
Non haberes potestatem adversum me ullam,
“You would not have any authority over me,
unless it were given to you from above.
he who has handed me over to you has the greater sin.”
Et exinde quærebat Pilatus dimittere eum.
And from then on, Pilate was seeking to release him.
But the Jews were crying out, saying:
you are no friend of Caesar.
Omnis enim qui se regem facit, contradicit Cæsari.
For anyone who makes himself a king contradicts Caesar.”
Pilatus autem cum audisset hos sermones,
Now when Pilate had heard these words,
and he sat down in the seat of judgment,
in a place which is called the Pavement,
but in Hebrew, it is called the Elevation.
Now it was the preparation day of the Passover,
And he said to the Jews,
Tunc ergo tradidit eis illum ut crucifigeretur.
he then handed him over to them to be crucified.
And they took Jesus and led him away.
Et bajulans sibi crucem exivit in eum,
he went forth to the place which is called Calvary,
but in Hebrew it is called the Place of the Skull.

Then Pilate also wrote a title,
and he set it above the cross.
Hunc ergo titulum multi Judæorum legerunt:
many of the Jews read this title,
for the place where Jesus was crucified was close to the city.
And it was written in Hebrew,
Then the high priests of the Jews said to Pilate:
Then the soldiers, when they had crucified him,
acceperunt vestimenta ejus (et fecerunt quatuor partes,
took his garments, and they made four parts,
one part to each soldier, and the tunic.
Erat autem tunica inconsutilis, desuper contexta per totum.
But the tunic was seamless, woven from above throughout the whole.
Then they said to one another, “Let us not cut it,
but instead let us cast lots over it,
sed sortiamur de illa cujus sit. Ut Scriptura impleretur,
to see whose it will be.” This was so that the Scripture would be fulfilled,
dicens: Partiti sunt vestimenta mea sibi:
saying: “They have distributed my garments among themselves,
et in vestem meam miserunt sortem.
and for my vesture they have cast lots.”
And indeed, the soldiers did these things.
Stabant autem juxta crucem Jesu mater ejus,
And standing beside the cross of Jesus were his mother,
when Jesus had seen his mother
and the disciple whom he loved standing near,
Next, he said to the disciple,
Et ex illa hora accepit eam discipulus in sua.
And from that hour, the disciple accepted her as his own.
Postea sciens Jesus quia omnia consummata sunt,
After this, Jesus knew that all had been accomplished,
so in order that the Scripture might be completed,
Vas ergo erat positum aceto plenum.
And there was a container placed there, full of vinegar.
Illi autem spongiam plenam aceto, hyssopo circumponentes,
Then, placing a sponge full of vinegar around hyssop,
they brought it to his mouth.
Then Jesus, when he had received the vinegar,
And bowing down his head, he surrendered his spirit.
Judæi ergo (quoniam parasceve erat) ut non remanerent in cruce corpora sabbato (erat enim magnus dies ille sabbati),
Then the Jews, because it was the preparation day, so that the bodies would not remain upon the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a great day),
rogaverunt Pilatum ut frangerentur eorum crura,
they petitioned Pilate in order that their legs might be broken,
and they might be taken away.
and, indeed, they broke the legs of the first one,
et alterius, qui crucifixus est cum eo.
and of the other who was crucified with him.
But after they had approached Jesus,
when they saw that he was already dead,
they did not break his legs.
sed unus militum lancea latus ejus aperuit,
one of the soldiers opened his side with a lance,
and immediately there went out blood and water.
And he who saw this has offered testimony,
Et ille scit quia vera dicit:
And he knows that he speaks the truth,
so that you also may believe.
Facta sunt enim hæc ut Scriptura impleretur:
For these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled:
“You shall not break a bone of him.”
“They shall look upon him, whom they have pierced.”

Post hæc autem rogavit Pilatum Joseph ab Arimathæa (eo quod esset discipulus Jesu, occultus autem propter metum Judæorum), ut tolleret corpus Jesu. Et permisit Pilatus. Venit ergo, et tulit corpus Jesu.

Then, after these things, Joseph from Arimathea, (because he was a disciple of Jesus, but a secret one for fear of the Jews) petitioned Pilate so that he might take away the body of Jesus. And Pilate gave permission. Therefore, he went and took away the body of Jesus.

Therefore, they took the body of Jesus,
et ligaverunt illud linteis cum aromatibus,
and they bound it with linen cloths and the aromatic spices,
just as it is the manner of the Jews to bury.
Erat autem in loco, ubi crucifixus est, hortus:
Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden,
and in the garden there was a new tomb,
in quo nondum quisquam positus erat.
in which no one had yet been laid.
